chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Buzay', from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyabah, from Imran ibn Mitham, from Abaya ibn Rabi' al-Asadi, who said:
I heard Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) say: 'How will you be when you remain without an Imam of guidance or a visible standard, when some of you turn away from the other with disdain?'

key_terms.يَبْرَأُ بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ: Some of you turn away from the other

ai.seo_question: What is the condition of the Shia during the occultation of the Imam according to Tusi?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from Imran ibn Maytham warns of the 'Test of the Occultation' (*Balā' al-Ghayba*), where the absence of the visible Imam leads to fragmentation and mutual disavowal among the Shia. It underscores the critical role of the Imam as the guarantor of communal unity and religious clarity, a theme central to Twelver eschatology.
